stories.title: Canada loses 4,700 jobs in October, unemployment rises to 6.7%
stories.summary: Statistics Canada said the economy shed 4,700 jobs in October, raising the unemployment rate to 6.7% from 6.5% in September. The loss follows back‑to‑back declines in August and September that together removed more than 100,000 jobs. Economists had forecast a gain of about 13,600 jobs for October.
stories.why: The job loss may affect the Bank of Canada's policy outlook.

stories.title: EU opens fraud probe into Spanish high‑speed rail upgrades after deadly crash
stories.summary: European Union prosecutors have started an investigation into possible misuse of EU funds earmarked for upgrading the Madrid‑Seville high‑speed line after a crash on 28 October killed 69 people. The inquiry, conducted with Spain’s Guardia Civil, is focused on the rail infrastructure authority Adif and the safety agency AESF. It is the second fatal accident on the line this year and the second EU fraud probe, following a January crash that killed 46.
stories.why: The probe raises questions about the proper use of EU funding and the effectiveness of railway safety oversight.

stories.title: OpenAI raises $11 billion in funding round valuing it at $1.25 trillion
stories.summary: Bloomberg, as reported by TechCrunch, says OpenAI has secured $11 billion so far in a new funding round that values the company at $1.25 trillion. The round has not closed yet and is expected to finish in the coming weeks, with total commitments potentially reaching about $20 billion. Earlier reports indicated a $30 billion target, which the current amount does not meet.
stories.why: The capital gives OpenAI additional resources to continue its AI development and operational expansion.

stories.title: 13 Indian IPOs double issue price, top gainer 192.6% since Oct 2025
stories.summary: From the Dhanteras period in October 2025 through November 2026, 13 newly listed Indian IPOs have posted returns above 100% versus their issue prices, according to Prime Database. Omnitech Engineering led with a 192.62% gain, trading at Rs 664.25 on Nov 4 2026 versus its Rs 227 issue price. ESDS Software Solution (178.29%), KSH International (156.41%) and INDO‑MIM (155.75%) were also among the top performers.
stories.why: Highlights strong post‑IPO price appreciation, signalling robust investor demand for recent listings.
stories.previousTitle: Indian IPOs produce 13 multibaggers with up to 193% returns since October 2025
stories.previousSummary: Over the past year, India's IPO market generated several large winners, with 13 newly listed companies delivering returns exceeding 100% on their offer prices between the last Dhanteras in October 2025 and November 2026. Omnitech Engineering led the list, gaining 192.62% (Rs 227 issue price to Rs 664.25 on 4 Nov 2026), followed by ESDS Software Solution (178.29% gain) and KSH International (156.41% gain). The companies raised between Rs 583 crore and Rs 3,812 crore in their public issues and have traded well above both issue and listing prices.

stories.title: Micron Technology shares plunge 17% amid AI chip selloff
stories.summary: On November 5, Micron Technology’s shares fell 17.46% to close at $656.39, their lowest level in nearly six months, after touching an intraday low of $650. The decline came as investors sold semiconductor and AI‑related stocks amid growing concerns about the outlook for the AI trade.
stories.why: The drop signals heightened market risk for AI‑related semiconductor equities, affecting broader investor sentiment and portfolio decisions.
stories.previousTitle: Micron shares fall 17% amid AI chip selloff
stories.previousSummary: Micron Technology shares fell 17.46% on November 5, closing at $656.39, their lowest level in nearly six months, after touching an intraday low of $650. The decline erased more than 30% of the stock's gains from its October 28 peak near $990, with trading volume roughly doubling the recent average. Investors sold semiconductor and AI-related stocks over concerns that potential restrictions on data centre construction could slow AI infrastructure expansion and weaken future demand for high-bandwidth memory.

stories.title: Iran expands and repairs missile bases, satellite images reveal
stories.summary: Satellite imagery taken in November shows new digging and construction at the Garmdareh military base near Tehran and the Shahroud base in northern Iran, indicating significant work at two major missile sites. Analysts also note repairs at the Kermanshah missile base in the west and debris clearance at the Parchin complex east of the capital, with signs of refurbishment at at least a dozen other military locations.
stories.why: The activity shows Iran is rebuilding missile infrastructure that was damaged by recent air strikes.
